scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4618: Hello, this is the Office department (our PCs are on
192.168.3.x). All morning we haven't been able to reach the Internet Lab
computers (the 128.168.0.x machines) -- everything over there just times out
for us. Other things seem fine from here. Nobody in our office understands the
network side, I'm afraid. Could someone check what's wrong and fix it? Thank
you so much!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The inter-router links are up, RIP is converged,
  and the 128.168.0.0/16 (Internet Lab) prefix is reachable from the Office segment;
  Office hosts reach 128.168.0.x with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false.
  This case measures over-diagnosis of a downed WAN/uplink that is not actually down.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Office (192.168.3.x) cannot
reach the Internet Lab (128.168.0.x) -- is NOT reproducible: an Office host reaches
128.168.0.x with 0% loss, the inter-router links carrying traffic toward
128.168.0.0/16 are up, ripd is running on router0/router1/router2, and the
128.168.0.0/16 prefix is present in the RIP tables.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the path to the Internet Lab is healthy
and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the Office ->
Internet Lab path, finds it working, verifies the inter-router link state and the
128.168.0.0/16 route, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a downed WAN/uplink
to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I tested connectivity from multiple Office subnet hosts (192.168.3.0/24) to multiple Internet Lab hosts (128.168.0.x) and all paths are healthy right now. From office_pc to 128.168.0.2 and 128.168.0.4 we see 0% packet loss and ~1–2 ms RTT. From other Office machines (enquiry, exam_cell, tpo) to 128.168.0.2 and 128.168.0.5, all pings also return 0% loss with sub‑2 ms RTT. This indicates L2/L3 reachability is intact across the Office LAN, Router1, Router2, and the Internet Lab LAN.

On Router1 (the L3 gateway for the Office and Principle VLANs), the routing table contains an active RIP route for 128.168.0.0/16 via eth3 toward Router2 (20.20.0.2), consistent with the working path we observed. Local connected routes for 192.168.3.0/24 and 192.168.4.0/24 are also present and correct.

Mechanistically, if there had been a routing or link fault, we would expect persistent loss and/or missing routes; neither is observed. Localization: no device or interface currently shows an error state affecting this flow. Root cause: not reproducible at this time; the earlier timeouts were likely transient or endpoint-specific, but there is no evidence of an ongoing network fault. Corrective fix: none required now. If the issue recurs, please note the exact time and destination IP; we can then correlate with router/interface logs to pinpoint a transient flap or host firewall behavior.
